title: Binary Tree Right Side View
pattern: Breadth-first search: last node of each level
statement: Imagine standing to the **right** of a binary tree. Return the values of the nodes you can see, from top to bottom.

example.why: Node 3 hides node 2, but nothing stands to the right of node 4 on the bottom level.

idea: From the right you see exactly one node per level: the **rightmost** one.
It is not enough to follow right children — a deeper node in the *left* subtree is visible when the right side is shorter.
So walk the tree level by level with a queue, and for each level record the **last** node taken out.

complexity.timeWhy: Every node passes through the queue once, and a deque removes its front item in O(1).
complexity.spaceWhy: The queue holds up to one full level.

steps.text: Our example: **`root = [1,2,3,4]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
We walk the tree **level by level**. Seen from the right, the visible node of each level is the last one in it.
